framework: Physically Coupled Digital Twin Fault Propagation Architecture

thermal_overheating.physical_mechanism: Cooling airflow reduction / heat rejection deficit causing thermal accumulation in cylinder head mass
thermal_overheating.governing_equation: C_th * d(CHT)/dt = Q_combustion - h_conv * A * (CHT - T_amb) - Q_cooling_deficit

injector_degradation.physical_mechanism: Fuel injector nozzle clogging / solenoid latency reducing mass fuel delivery per stroke to specific cylinder
observable_telemetry: MAP slightly increases as governor compensates

cylinder_misfire.physical_mechanism: Ignition spark failure or severe lean blowout preventing combustion in single cylinder
cylinder_misfire.governing_equation: eta_comb = 0 for cylinder i -> Brake Power = 3/4 * P_nominal - P_friction

lubrication_degradation.physical_mechanism: Oil pump pressure drop / viscosity shear thinning / oil cooler fouling

sensor_drift_and_bias.physical_mechanism: Thermocouple calibration drift or ADC reference shift without physical engine change
observable_telemetry: Single sensor deviates while cross-coupled sensors (EGT, OilT) remain nominal

sensor_dropout.physical_mechanism: Open circuit / CAN packet loss causing sensor reading to drop to zero or NaN
observable_telemetry: Instantaneous step to 0 or flatline rate of change

metadata_provenance.synthetic_data_disclaimer: Synthetic fault trajectories are physically grounded in thermo-fluid first principles and calibrated against NASA ACES nominal operating bounds. They are labeled as PROGNOSTIC / SIMULATION ESTIMATES and never conflated with real run-to-failure ground truth.
